name: @effectified/sharp
tagline: a builder that is also a Node stream

decisions.question: Which exported functions and classes does the facade offer?
decisions.why: every exported function or class that is async or yields a handle

decisions.question: Which method releases a Sharp, so acquiring one opens a scope? ("none" keeps it unscoped)
decisions.why: its type has no release method

decisions.question: Which events of Sharp does the facade offer as Streams? ("none" for none)
Which upstream failures become which tagged errors?
decisions.why: exported error classes, most specific first, then the catch-all SharpError carrying `code` (the source sets ERR_DLOPEN_DISABLED)

decisions.question: Which handles are provided as services (Context.Service with a layer)?
decisions.why: every offered export that acquires a releasable handle

decisions.question: Which revision of this upstream version is the facade?
decisions.why: engine 0.4.0: every Effect traced as `<Handle>.<method>` (Effect.fn: a span and a stack frame per call), a value upstream may not have as an Option, errors branded with upstream's codes as a `reason` union (Effect.catchReason) and `Failure` as the Schema of all of them, facades Equal by their upstream object, releases traced and a failed one logged, upstream's types re-exported by name and its plain values as they are, and the facade held to @effect/tsgo and the GritQL idioms; after its re-check: the 15 values sharp's CommonJS module hides from Node's named imports (`block`, `format`, `versions`...) no longer re-exported, which made the facade fail to import (each stays `Upstream.default.<name>`); a facade serialises and prints as its handle's name whatever upstream's own toJSON or toString show (neither wrapped), a handle it did not acquire has no release method, a secret's value is scrubbed from failures, the release is registered before a handle is wrapped, a release that fails as its scope closes is logged, and every entry point of the built facade imports in Node; after its third fix round: upstream's failure is kept only as a `Redacted` cause, never copied, walked or printed (`Redacted.value(error.cause)` reaches it), and an error's message and declared string fields are scrubbed of each secret of four characters or more given to the call, its codes never; after its sixth fix round: every failure of a stream's iteration is classified with the call's secrets (its iterator's making, each step, a step it cannot read), an acquired handle is released once by the scope (one a list holds twice, or one two calls hand back), and the facade checks that what each member gives agrees between its type and the runtime (`CheckedGives`); the callback overloads that return the image (`toBuffer(callback)`, `toFile(file, callback)`, `metadata(callback)`, `stats(callback)`), typed as returning its facade while the run time ran them as Effects, are left out beside their promise overloads; after its release checks: the scope releases what it acquired when it closes, whatever the user did with it (a user's own call of a release reaches upstream and changes nothing the scope does; the scope's later release that fails is logged as a warning), and an interrupted acquisition aborts upstream's call, waits for it and leaves what it gave to the scope, as Effect's `acquireRelease` does
